SearchAliases: the face you had before your parents were born
face before your parents were born
Senses.Explanation: The original face is a recurring public question for what is originally one's own; the records answer it with attributable words and actions while refusing to let any one reply become the headword's universal definition. Huineng asks Huiming, ‘Not thinking of good, not thinking of evil—right at such a moment, which is Elder Ming's original face?’ (不思善，不思惡，正恁麼時，阿那箇是明上座本來面目). Helin Tianshu Zhi later asks for ‘the original face before father and mother were born’ (如何是父母未生前本來面目), and Muyun Tongmen separately supplies the raised-fist response. Nanyue Jiqi Hongchu himself tells a departing monk, ‘Go to the time before father and mother were born and clarify the original face’ (去父母未生時，明取本來面目); after the record's anonymous question challenges the apparent conflict with his usual prohibition, Nanyue himself answers, ‘Alas! Misfortune for the teaching gate.’ Huanglong Huinan tells wayfarers to recognize the original face amid thorns and muddy water, while Tianru Weize tells his audience that each has an original face not yet recognized. At Jinsu, Shiche Tongcheng asks Qiyuan Xinggang, ‘What is your original face?’ and Qiyuan's separate reply is ‘eyebrows horizontal, nose straight.’ Baichi Yuan rejects an interlocutor's abstract reply by asking why so many principles were offered when he had asked for the original face (問汝本來面目，說許多道理作麼). Two headword-free replies preserve further full cases without pretending their respondents uttered the question: Fuchuan Hongjian closes his eyes and sticks out his tongue, then opens his eyes and repeats the gesture; Dongshan Liangjie answers a direct question with ‘not traveling the bird course.’ Dongshan's reply belongs inside the larger exchange in which he first instructs travel along the bird's trackless flight-course and rejects equating that travel with the original face. It therefore does not convert either traveling or not traveling into the dictionary definition.
Senses.Note: The apparatus-clean allowlist count is 1,320 hits across 264 texts. One sense remains warranted: the records ask for the same original face through many replies, gestures, corrections, and prohibitions, but those different responses do not name different referents. Dongshan's bird-course answer is case-scoped and deliberately preserved together with his opposite travel instruction; it neither redefines the headword as the bird course nor makes non-travel a universal prescription.

Occurrences.Kwic: 盧曰：不思善，不思惡，正恁麼時，阿那箇是明上座本來面目？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, fascicles 1–33 (五燈全書(第1卷-第33卷)) records Huineng asking Huiming which is Elder Ming's original face at the moment of not thinking good or evil.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師問：「如何是父母未生前本來面目？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Helin Tianshu Zhi (鶴林天樹植禪師語錄), Helin Tianshu Zhi himself asks Muyun Tongmen for the original face before father and mother were born. Muyun's later response is stored separately so the two actors are not fused.

Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Helin Tianshu Zhi (鶴林天樹植禪師語錄): Muyun Tongmen raises his fist when Helin Tianshu Zhi renews the request. This actor-pure, no-headword response preserves the full case but does not buy original-face depth.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰：「去父母未生時，明取本來面目。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Recorded Sayings of Nanyue Jiqi (南嶽繼起和尚語錄), Nanyue Jiqi Hongchu himself tells a monk leaving the hall to go to the time before father and mother were born and clarify the original face. The following anonymous challenge and Nanyue's response are kept separate.

Recorded Sayings of Nanyue Jiqi (南嶽繼起和尚語錄): after an anonymous monk challenges Nanyue Jiqi Hongchu about the apparent conflict between this instruction and his usual prohibition, Nanyue answers, ‘Alas! Misfortune for the teaching gate.’ This no-headword response preserves the actor-pure completion of the case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 行脚人須是荊棘林內坐大道場，向和泥合水處認取本來面目。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, fascicles 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), in the explicit Huanglong Huinan section, records Huanglong's hall statement that a wayfarer must recognize the original face amid thorns and muddy water.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只是汝諸人各各有箇本來面目，不曾認得這箇本來面目，直下與諸佛同體。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tianru Weize (天如惟則禪師語錄), in Tianru Weize's general address: Tianru tells the assembled beginners that each has an original face not yet recognized and immediately places it in his instruction.

Occurrences.Kwic: 粟問：「如何是你本來面目？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Qiyuan Xinggang of Fushi (伏獅祇園禪師語錄) recounts Qiyuan going to Jinsu to call on Shiche Tongcheng (金粟參石車和尚). In that continuing autobiographical case, the abbreviated Jinsu marker identifies Shiche Tongcheng as the person asking Qiyuan, ‘What is your original face?’ Qiyuan's response is stored separately so the question is not assigned to its respondent.

Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Qiyuan Xinggang of Fushi (伏獅祇園禪師語錄): Qiyuan Xinggang, the continuing autobiographical subject called ‘the master’ in the record, answers Shiche Tongcheng's original-face question, ‘eyebrows horizontal, nose straight.’ This actor-pure, no-headword response preserves the case but does not buy headword depth.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「問汝本來面目，說許多道理作麼？」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baichi (百癡禪師語錄), Baichi Yuan himself rejects the anonymous monk's abstract response by asking why he has offered so many principles when asked for his original face. Only Baichi's actor-pure headword turn is stored.

Collected Old Cases of the Lineage Gate (宗門拈古彙集), explicit Dongshan Liangjie section: Dongshan answers the anonymous original-face question, ‘not traveling the bird course.’ The headword belongs only to the questioner, so Dongshan's actor-pure reply is no-headword support and does not buy depth.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師閉目吐舌，又開目吐舌示之。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, fascicles 1–33 (五燈全書(第1卷-第33卷)), explicit Fuchuan Hongjian section: Fuchuan closes his eyes and sticks out his tongue, then opens his eyes and repeats the gesture. The anonymous monk uttered the headword question, so Fuchuan's actor-pure gesture is stored only as support.
